title: SQRTPI uses CRT pow(n*pi, 0.5) not IEEE sqrt, returns #NUM! for n*pi > DBL_MAX, and rejects logicals
statement: In Excel 16.0 builds 20026, 20430, and 20527, SQRTPI(number) rejects logicals with #VALUE!, rejects number < 0 with #NUM!, multiplies number * pi in binary64 (returning #NUM! once number * pi overflows DBL_MAX, starting at 0x7fd45f306dc9c883), and evaluates CRT pow(number * pi, 0.5) rather than IEEE sqrt. At =SQRTPI(1), Excel returns 1.7724538509055159 (0x3ffc5bf891b4ef6a), 1 ULP below exact sqrt(pi); at 0x7fd45f306dc9c882 it returns 0x5ff0000000000000 (1 ULP above IEEE sqrt).
basis: Measured across Excel 16.0 build 20026 (sqrtpi.rs pinned boundary tests), build 20430 (1,224/1,224 full-bank and 120/120 pinned SQRTPI rows), and 16.0.20527.20088 in prefix_metadata (row 209) and functions-fn4-arguments (qa047).

correct.how: 100-digit decimal sqrt(pi), rounded to nearest binary64

repros.recorded_in: Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA

correct.how: Exact sqrt(0x7fd45f306dc9c882 * pi) < 2^512, rounded to nearest binary64
